title: Over-ear headphone: parametric design template (theory-only)
description: A 40 mm dynamic driver in an over-ear (circumaural) cup, closed-back by default, open-back as an option. Modelled: the front cavity as a cylinder between the driver and the ear, sealed by an impermeable (protein-leather) pad except for a leak gap around its inner edge; a damping cloth over the driver's rear openings, with the air space between it and the diaphragm; behind it either a closed rear cavity vented through holes that can carry a mesh, or an open grille radiating into the room; the ear load, the IEC 60318-4 simulator (a flat-plate fixture) or the ITU-T P.57 Type 4.3 ear. Anchors: driver defaults are the Tymphany HPD-40N16PET00-32 primary set (docs/spec-errata.md E5); the front volume (47.5 cm3) lies in the range published for circumaural cups (about 50 cm3 in Bose US 6,597,792; 62 and 79 cm3 with uncompressed pads in Focal US 12,513,448). Estimates: the pad and cup geometry, the rear volume, the vent and the damping cloth; tolerances are datasheet values where stated and estimates otherwise. Not modelled: the pinna and concha, a porous (velour) pad path, the front chamber's transverse modes and diaphragm break-up, so above about 1 kHz (where the shading starts) the curves are the lumped model's, not a prediction of a real cup. docs/templates.md gives the sources and what the defaults produce.

driver_diameter_mm.label: Effective diaphragm diameter
driver_diameter_mm.description: Diameter of a circle of area Sd; the cross-section draws the diaphragm this wide.

driver_Le_uH.label: Coil inductance Le
driver_Le_uH.description: Near zero for most headphone drivers (spec Section 4); a few hundred microhenries would falsely roll off the treble of a 32 ohm driver.

front_radius_mm.label: Cup inner radius
front_radius_mm.description: Radius of the cylindrical space between the driver and the ear; also the pad's inner edge, which sets the leak perimeter. 27.5 mm (a 55 mm opening) is an estimate for a pad that fits around an adult pinna.

front_depth_mm.label: Driver-to-ear depth
front_depth_mm.description: Distance from the diaphragm to the head or fixture plate with the pad compressed (estimate). With the default radius the front volume is 47.5 cm3, within the published range for circumaural cups (docs/templates.md).

leak_gap_mm.label: Pad leak gap (0 = sealed)
leak_gap_mm.description: Mean gap between the pad and the head or fixture, as a thermoviscous slit around the pad's inner edge. Fit varies this from person to person.

damping_rayl.label: Damping cloth behind the driver (0 = none)
damping_rayl.description: Specific flow resistance, MKS rayl, of the felt or non-woven cloth over the driver's rear openings, between the diaphragm and the rear cavity or grille. It damps the resonance of the diaphragm on the cup's air springs. 600 rayl is the engineered-textile grade of the materials database (textile_acoustic_600, unverified); the value for a given product is not public.

tolerance.source: estimate (felt and non-woven; meshes are held to 10-15 %)

damping_area_cm2.label: Open area under the damping cloth
damping_area_cm2.description: Total area of the driver's rear openings that the cloth covers (estimate). The acoustic resistance is the cloth's rayl value over this area.

driver_back_volume_cm3.label: Air space behind the diaphragm
driver_back_volume_cm3.description: Volume between the diaphragm and the driver's rear openings, inside the driver frame (estimate). Without a damping cloth it opens straight into the rear cavity or grille.

vent_mesh_rayl.label: Vent mesh resistance (0 = open hole)
vent_mesh_rayl.description: Specific flow resistance of a mesh covering each vent, MKS rayl (160 is the Saati Acoustex grade the spec cites).

grille_rayl.label: Open-back grille resistance
grille_rayl.description: Specific flow resistance of the grille and its fabric over the diaphragm area, MKS rayl (used when the back is open).

choices.label: ITU-T P.57 Type 4.3 ear (canal and drum)

source_impedance_ohm.label: Amplifier output impedance
source_impedance_ohm.description: 0 ohm ideal, below 1 ohm portable, 10 ohm desktop, 120 ohm the legacy IEC 61938 figure.

drive_mW.label: Drive power into the rated impedance
drive_mW.description: Every level states its drive: this is the power into the rated impedance (1 mW is the usual sensitivity reference). Warnings such as vent velocity and excursion are checked at this drive.
